what: Rockwell Automation makes the control systems that run factories: programmable controllers, drives, sensors, safety systems and the software that ties them together, sold mainly under the Allen-Bradley brand.
customers: Food and beverage, car, life sciences, semiconductor, warehousing and energy manufacturers, mostly in North America.
money: drives, motion control, safety and industrial components
moat: Allen-Bradley equipment is the North American factory standard, and engineers trained on its programming environment design new plants around it.
risks: Factory capital spending has been weak for two years
Revenue has been flat over three years
Tariffs and supply chain shifts affect customers' investment decisions
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 23% with a 50% gross margin
Reshoring of manufacturing to North America is exactly its market
Revenue grew about 8% last year as orders recovered
watch: Order growth and the book-to-bill ratio.
